verdict.rationale: Calendly documents scopes that limit which resources an integration can read or modify. Credentials can be issued as personal access tokens or as OAuth 2.1 access tokens with PKCE, and the MCP server uses Dynamic Client Registration so an agent can get OAuth credentials without a pre-registered app. Scope detail is thin: one sentence, with no scope list and no statement that personal access tokens can be scoped. Missing for 10: an enumerated scope catalog, explicit scoping of personal access tokens, agent-specific least-privilege guidance, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can issue scoped/least-privilege API credentials for an agent

citations.quote: Scopes control which Calendly resources your integration can read or modify.
Use a personal access token to authenticate an internal or private application with the Calendly API v2.
Then use the OAuth authorization code flow with PKCE to get an access token for each user.
Calendly MCP uses Dynamic Client Registration (DCR), which means **you do not need to pre-register an OAuth application**
